# Model and source

Tanigawara 2012 describes how the Japanese clinical dose of the
des-F(6)-quinolone garenoxacin (400 mg orally once daily) was chosen at the end
of phase II from an interim population PK model plus Monte Carlo simulation,
and then confirmed with phase III PK/PD data. The paper contributes four model
files, all documented in this one article:

| Model file | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Tanigawara_2012_garenoxacin` | Final phase I-III one-compartment popPK model (NONMEM VI FOCE-I) |
| `Tanigawara_2012_garenoxacin_interim` | Interim end-of-phase-II popPK "Model 2" (NONMEM V FO), used for the Monte Carlo dose selection |
| `Tanigawara_2012_garenoxacin_cure` | Phase III logistic regression of clinical cure on log10(fAUC0-24/MIC) |
| `Tanigawara_2012_garenoxacin_cure_cart` | The same data with fAUC0-24/MIC dichotomised at the CART split of 28 h |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tanigawara_2012_garenoxacin"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00228-011-1095-3> (open access, PMC3249185)

The electronic supplement holds only the goodness-of-fit plots of the final
model (Supplementary Fig. 1). A EuropePMC search on 2026-11-19 found no
erratum or correction.

```{r models}
mod_final <- readModelDb("Tanigawara_2012_garenoxacin")
mod_interim <- readModelDb("Tanigawara_2012_garenoxacin_interim")
mod_cure <- readModelDb("Tanigawara_2012_garenoxacin_cure")
mod_cart <- readModelDb("Tanigawara_2012_garenoxacin_cure_cart")
ui_final <- rxode2::rxode(mod_final)
ui_interim <- rxode2::rxode(mod_interim)
```

# Population

The PK data come from five Japanese studies (Tanigawara 2012 Tables 1-2): three
phase I studies in 49 healthy volunteers (100-600 mg single doses, 200 or 400
mg once daily for 7-14 days, and a fed/fasted 400 mg study; 1,321 samples), a
phase II study in 55 patients with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) or
secondary infection of chronic respiratory disease (SICRD) given 200 or 400 mg
once daily for 7-14 days (75 samples), and a phase III study in 133 patients
with mild or moderate SICRD given 400 mg once daily for 10 days (346 samples).

* Interim model (phases I-II): 104 subjects, 77 men, age 40.0 +/- 20.4 years
  (20-74), weight 58.5 +/- 10.4 kg (34-83), Cockcroft-Gault CLCR 102.4 +/- 29.7
  mL/min (34.4-178.7).
* Final model (phases I-III): 237 subjects, 164 men; the phase III patients
  were older (66.3 +/- 14.8 years, 19-94), lighter (52.7 +/- 13.0 kg, 33-120)
  and had lower renal function (CLCR 71.1 +/- 29.4 mL/min, 19.3-199.2).
* Exposure-response: the 66 phase III patients with an isolated causative
  organism and MIC; 58 were cured (87.9%).

```{r population}
str(ui_final$population[c("n_subjects", "n_studies", "age_range", "weight_range", "sex_female_pct")])
```

| Final `e_sex_vc` (theta6), GEN = 1 male | 6.98 L | Table 4; GEN coding Table 3 footnote a |
| Final `lka` | 2.14 1/h | Table 4 |

| Interim `propSd` = sqrt(sigma^2) | sqrt(0.0645) = 0.254 | Table 4 (CV 25.4%) |

# Typical-value checks against Figure 2 and the Results text

Figure 2 and the Results report exposure at 400 mg once daily from the
population-mean parameters of the final model, "varying one covariate within
the particular range while all other covariates were kept at their mean
value". The pooled means are CLCR 85 mL/min and weight 55 kg (the centring
values of the model), and 164 of 237 subjects were men, so the "mean" sex
indicator is SEXF = 73/237.

```{r typical-scenarios}
sexf_mean <- 73 / 237
scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,            ~CRCL, ~WT,
  "Mean covariates",       85,  55,
  "CLCR 20 mL/min",        20,  55,
  "CLCR 49 mL/min",        49,  55,
  "CLCR 50 mL/min",        50,  55,
  "CLCR 79 mL/min",        79,  55,
  "CLCR 80 mL/min",        80,  55,
  "CLCR 110 mL/min",      110,  55,
  "WT 60 kg",              85,  60,
  "WT 100 kg",             85, 100
) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()), SEXF = sexf_mean, treatment = scenario)

ss_dose <- scen |>
  mutate(time = 0, amt = 400, ii = 24, ss = 1L, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
ss_obs <- scen |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 24, by = 0.05)) |>
  mutate(amt = 0, ii = 0, ss = 0L, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
ss_events <- bind_rows(ss_dose, ss_obs) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, ii, ss, evid, cmt, CRCL, WT, SEXF)

sim_tv <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(ui_final), events = ss_events,
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, ssRtol = 1e-10, ssAtol = 1e-12,
  maxsteps = 1e6, returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  left_join(select(scen, id, treatment), by = "id")

tv <- sim_tv |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(cl_Lh = first(cl), AUC_closed = 400 / first(cl), Cmax = max(Cc), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(tv, digits = 2)
```

The Results text gives the AUC0-24 at the band limits (normal CLCR 80-110
mL/min: 96-105; mild impairment 50-79 mL/min: 105-117; moderate impairment
20-49 mL/min: 117-132 ug*h/mL), the population mean (104 ug*h/mL, Figure 2;
104 ug*h/mL also in the Discussion) and the population-mean Cmax (7.75 ug/mL,
Figure 2). The closed-form steady-state AUC = dose / CL is exact for this
linear model.

```{r typical-checks}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,          ~metric, ~published,
  "Mean covariates",   "AUC",   104,
  "Mean covariates",   "Cmax",  7.75,
  "CLCR 20 mL/min",    "AUC",   132,
  "CLCR 49 mL/min",    "AUC",   117,
  "CLCR 50 mL/min",    "AUC",   117,
  "CLCR 79 mL/min",    "AUC",   105,
  "CLCR 80 mL/min",    "AUC",   105,
  "CLCR 110 mL/min",   "AUC",   96
)
tv_long <- tv |>
  select(treatment, AUC = AUC_closed, Cmax) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-treatment, names_to = "metric", values_to = "model")
tv_check <- inner_join(published, tv_long, by = c("treatment", "metric")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model - published) / published)
stopifnot(nrow(tv_check) == nrow(published))
tv_check |>
  dplyr::rename(Scenario = treatment, Metric = metric, Published = published,
                Model = model, "% diff" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# Deterministic typical-value quantities against values the paper prints to
# 2-3 significant figures; a transcription error in any theta moves these by
# more than the rounding of the printed value.
stopifnot(all(abs(tv_check$pct_diff) < 1.5))

# 'In a comparison by body weight between a 100-kg patient and 60-kg patient,
# the AUC0-24 and Cmax decreased by 0.86-fold'
auc_ratio <- tv$AUC_closed[tv$treatment == "WT 100 kg"] / tv$AUC_closed[tv$treatment == "WT 60 kg"]
auc_ratio
stopifnot(abs(auc_ratio - 0.86) < 0.01)
```

The AUC ratio for 100 kg against 60 kg reproduces the reported 0.86-fold. The
corresponding Cmax ratio is
`r round(tv$Cmax[tv$treatment == "WT 100 kg"] / tv$Cmax[tv$treatment == "WT 60 kg"], 2)`,
because the larger V/F of heavier patients lowers Cmax more than AUC; the paper
quotes a single 0.86-fold figure for both.

## PKNCA on the typical-value steady-state profiles

```{r pknca-typical}
conc_tv <- sim_tv |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
dose_tv <- scen |> transmute(id, treatment, time = 0, amt = 400)

nca_tv <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_tv, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_tv, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))

ref_tv <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("Mean covariates", "Mean covariates", "CLCR 20 mL/min",
                "CLCR 49 mL/min", "CLCR 79 mL/min", "CLCR 110 mL/min"),
  PPTESTCD = c("cmax", "auclast", "auclast", "auclast", "auclast", "auclast"),
  PPORRES = c(7.75, 104, 132, 117, 105, 96)
)
tbl_tv <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_tv, ref_tv, by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", auclast = "ug*h/mL")
)
knitr::kable(tbl_tv, caption = "Typical-value steady-state NCA at 400 mg once daily (final model) against Figure 2 and the Results text.")
```

# Simulated phase III cohort (final model)

A virtual cohort shaped like the 133 phase III patients (Table 2: weight 52.7
+/- 13.0 kg, 33-120; CLCR 71.1 +/- 29.4 mL/min, 19.3-199.2; 87 of 133 men)
receives 400 mg once daily for 10 days. Weight and CLCR are drawn from
log-normal distributions with the published means and SDs, truncated to the
observed ranges, independently of each other (the paper gives no joint
distribution).

```{r cohort-helpers}
# Log-normal draws with a given arithmetic mean and SD, truncated to [lo, hi].
rlnorm_trunc <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  s2 <- log(1 + (sd / mean)^2)
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- rlnorm(4 * n, log(mean) - s2 / 2, sqrt(s2))
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lo & x <= hi])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}
```

```{r cohort-sim}
set.seed(2012)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = rlnorm_trunc(n_sub, 52.7, 13.0, 33, 120),
  CRCL = rlnorm_trunc(n_sub, 71.1, 29.4, 19.3, 199.2),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 46 / 133),
  treatment = "400 mg QD"
)

dose_times <- seq(0, 216, by = 24)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 240, by = 1), 216 + seq(0, 24, by = 0.25))))
ev_p3 <- bind_rows(
  cohort |> tidyr::crossing(time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 400, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  cohort |> tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, WT, CRCL, SEXF)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2012)
sim_p3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_final, events = ev_p3, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  left_join(select(cohort, id, treatment), by = "id")
```

```{r vpc-day10, fig.cap = "Simulated 400 mg once-daily profile on day 10 in a phase III-like cohort (5th, 50th, 95th percentiles of the individual predictions). Compare with the right-hand panel of Figure 1 of Tanigawara 2012, whose simulated median peaks near 7.5 ug/mL about 2 h after the dose and falls to about 2 ug/mL at 24 h."}
vpc <- sim_p3 |>
  filter(time >= 216) |>
  mutate(tad = time - 216) |>
  group_by(tad) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc, aes(tad)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 6)) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose on day 10 (h)", y = "Garenoxacin plasma concentration (ug/mL)")
```

## PKNCA on the simulated cohort (day 10)

Figure 6 of Tanigawara 2012 shows box plots of the individual AUC0-24 and Cmax
of the 133 phase III patients, split by adverse-event status. The medians read
from the figure are about 113 and 115 ug*h/mL (AUC0-24) and about 8.4 and 8.8
ug/mL (Cmax); the reference values below are the midpoints, 114 ug*h/mL and
8.6 ug/mL.

```{r pknca-p3}
conc_p3 <- sim_p3 |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time >= 216) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
dose_p3 <- cohort |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = dose_times) |>
  transmute(id, treatment, time, amt = 400)

nca_p3 <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_p3, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_p3, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 216, end = 240, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))
ref_p3 <- data.frame(treatment = "400 mg QD", cmax = 8.6, auclast = 114)
tbl_p3 <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_p3, ref_p3, by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", auclast = "ug*h/mL")
)
knitr::kable(tbl_p3, caption = "Simulated day-10 NCA (median of 200 subjects) against the Figure 6 phase III medians (digitised).")

res_p3 <- as.data.frame(nca_p3$result)
med_auc <- median(res_p3$PPORRES[res_p3$PPTESTCD == "auclast"])
med_cmax <- median(res_p3$PPORRES[res_p3$PPTESTCD == "cmax"])
# Cohort medians: a mis-transcribed clearance, volume or unit conversion moves
# them by tens of percent; covariate sampling and digitisation stay well
# inside 15%.
stopifnot(abs(med_auc / 114 - 1) < 0.15, abs(med_cmax / 8.6 - 1) < 0.15)
```

# Interim model: trough above the MPC (Figure 4)

The end-of-phase-II Monte Carlo simulations used Model 2 with CLCR "randomly
re-sampled from real CLCR values (34.4-133.2 ml/min, n = 55)" of the phase II
patients, whose CLCR was 84.6 +/- 24.8 mL/min. The individual values are not
published, so here the 55-patient distribution is represented by 200 evenly
spaced quantiles of a normal distribution with that mean and SD, truncated to
the published range. The target is a trough above the mutant prevention
concentration of 1 ug/mL.

The published curve is very steep (day 1: about 0% at 200 mg, 23% at 250 mg,
81.4% at 300 mg and 100% from 350 mg), which matches a simulation in which only
CLCR varies and every other parameter is at its typical value. The chunk
below reproduces that (typical values, `zeroRe()`), and also shows the same
calculation with the between-subject variability of Model 2 switched on.

```{r fig4-setup}
p_grid <- (seq_len(200) - 0.5) / 200
a <- pnorm((34.4 - 84.6) / 24.8)
b <- pnorm((133.2 - 84.6) / 24.8)
crcl_grid <- 84.6 + 24.8 * qnorm(a + (b - a) * p_grid)

doses_fig4 <- c(100, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400, 600)
trough_times <- c(Day1 = 24, Day5 = 120, Day10 = 240) - 1e-4

subj4 <- tidyr::expand_grid(dose = doses_fig4, CRCL = crcl_grid) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()))
ev4 <- bind_rows(
  subj4 |> tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 216, by = 24)) |>
    mutate(amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  subj4 |> tidyr::crossing(time = unname(trough_times)) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, CRCL)

trough_prob <- function(sim, subj) {
  sim |>
    left_join(select(subj, id, dose), by = "id") |>
    mutate(day = names(trough_times)[match(round(time, 3), round(unname(trough_times), 3))]) |>
    group_by(dose, day) |>
    summarise(pct_above = 100 * mean(Cc > 1), .groups = "drop")
}

sim4_tv <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui_interim), events = ev4,
                           returnType = "data.frame")
fig4_tv <- trough_prob(sim4_tv, subj4)

# Same calculation with the Table 3 centring of 85 mL/min instead of 102:
# (CRCL - 85) equals ((CRCL + 17) - 102), so shifting the covariate by +17
# evaluates the alternative reading without editing the model.
sim4_85 <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui_interim),
                           events = mutate(ev4, CRCL = CRCL + 17),
                           returnType = "data.frame")
fig4_85 <- trough_prob(sim4_85, subj4)
```

```{r fig4-iiv}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(4)
sim4_iiv <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_interim, events = ev4, returnType = "data.frame")
fig4_iiv <- trough_prob(sim4_iiv, subj4)
```

```{r fig4-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Tanigawara 2012: probability that the garenoxacin trough exceeds the 1 ug/mL MPC on days 1, 5 and 10 (interim Model 2). Solid: typical values with only CLCR varying (the published construction); dashed: with the Model 2 between-subject variability."}
fig4 <- bind_rows(
  mutate(fig4_tv, sim = "Typical values, CLCR varying"),
  mutate(fig4_iiv, sim = "With between-subject variability")
)
ggplot(fig4, aes(dose, pct_above, colour = day, linetype = sim)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Dose (mg)", y = "Probability of trough above MPC (%)",
       colour = NULL, linetype = NULL)
```

```{r fig4-check}
fig4_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~day,    ~published,
  200,   "Day1",  0,
  250,   "Day1",  23.5,
  300,   "Day1",  81.4,
  350,   "Day1",  100,
  200,   "Day5",  38,
  250,   "Day5",  91,
  300,   "Day5",  100
)
fig4_cmp <- fig4_pub |>
  left_join(rename(fig4_tv, centred_102 = pct_above), by = c("dose", "day")) |>
  left_join(rename(fig4_85, centred_85 = pct_above), by = c("dose", "day")) |>
  left_join(rename(fig4_iiv, with_iiv = pct_above), by = c("dose", "day"))
stopifnot(nrow(fig4_cmp) == nrow(fig4_pub), !anyNA(fig4_cmp))
fig4_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg)" = dose, Day = day,
    "Published (%)" = published,
    "Typical, CLCR - 102 (%)" = centred_102,
    "Typical, CLCR - 85 (%)" = centred_85,
    "With IIV, CLCR - 102 (%)" = with_iiv
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Figure 4 (digitised; 81.4% at 300 mg on day 1 is quoted in the Results).")

# Deterministic (quantile grid, typical values): no Monte Carlo noise.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig4_cmp$centred_102 - fig4_cmp$published) < 10))
```

With CLCR centred at 102 mL/min (Table 4) the typical-value construction
reproduces every digitised point of Figure 4 to within about 7 percentage
points
(`r round(fig4_tv$pct_above[fig4_tv$dose == 300 & fig4_tv$day == "Day1"], 1)`%
against the quoted 81.4% at 300 mg on day 1; the residual gap reflects the
quantile-grid stand-in for the 55 real CLCR values). Centring at 85 mL/min
(the Model 2 row of Table 3) gives
`r round(fig4_85$pct_above[fig4_85$dose == 300 & fig4_85$day == "Day1"], 1)`%
at that point and misses the 250 mg and day-5 200 mg points by 18-25
percentage points, so the packaged interim model uses 102. With the Model 2
between-subject variability the curve is much flatter than the published one,
which is consistent with a simulation that held every parameter except CLCR
at its typical value.

# Interim model: fAUC0-24/MIC target attainment (Figure 3)

Figure 3 gives the probability that fAUC0-24/MIC exceeds 30 h at steady state
for 10,000 simulated AUC and MIC pairs per pathogen. The full MIC
distributions of the 1994-1997 Japanese isolates are not published (Table 2
gives only MIC90 and range), so Figure 3 and the Monte Carlo columns of
Table 7 cannot be regenerated. The chunk below instead shows the attainment
for fixed MICs, using the steady-state AUC0-24 = dose / CL/F of the interim
model over the same CLCR grid and fu = 0.25.

```{r fig3}
fu <- 0.25
cl_grid <- (66.7 + 0.167 * (crcl_grid - 102)) * 60 / 1000
pta <- tidyr::expand_grid(dose = c(100, 200, 400, 600, 800),
                          MIC = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.39, 0.78, 3.13)) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(pta = 100 * mean(fu * dose / cl_grid / MIC > 30)) |>
  ungroup()
pta |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = MIC, values_from = pta, names_prefix = "MIC ") |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg)" = dose) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Typical-value attainment (%) of fAUC0-24/MIC > 30 h by fixed MIC (ug/mL).")

# 'With a dose of >= 100 mg, the probability of 100% attainment could be
# expected for MSSA, ..., H. influenzae, and M. catarrhalis' -- MIC90 values
# of 0.0125-0.10 ug/mL (Table 2).
stopifnot(pta$pta[pta$dose == 100 & pta$MIC == 0.1] == 100)
```

The closed form here uses the model's own typical CL/F; the cross-check below
confirms it equals the `cl` the interim model computes.

```{r fig3-crosscheck}
cl_model <- sim4_tv |>
  select(id, cl) |>
  left_join(select(subj4, id, CRCL), by = "id") |>
  distinct(CRCL, cl)
stopifnot(max(abs(cl_model$cl / ((66.7 + 0.167 * (cl_model$CRCL - 102)) * 0.06) - 1)) < 1e-8)
```

# Clinical-cure exposure-response (Figure 5, Tables 5-6)

Both cure models are static: the total steady-state AUC0-24 and the patient's
MIC are supplied as covariate columns, one row per evaluation.

```{r er-helper}
er_eval <- function(model, cov) {
  ev <- cov |> mutate(id = 1L, time = seq_len(n()), amt = 0, evid = 0L)
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == nrow(cov))
  s$prob_clinical_success
}
```

Figure 5 plots the continuous logistic fit against fAUC0-24/MIC on a log axis.
With MIC = 1 ug/mL the unbound ratio is 0.25 x AUC, so the covariate grid
below spans fAUC0-24/MIC from 1 to 1000 h.

```{r fig5, fig.cap = "Replicates the fitted curve of Figure 5 of Tanigawara 2012: probability of clinical cure against fAUC0-24/MIC (continuous logistic model), with the CART-split model as a step."}
ratio_grid <- 10^seq(0, 3, length.out = 121)
cov_grid <- data.frame(AUC_GARENOXACIN = ratio_grid / 0.25, MIC = 1)
er_curve <- tibble::tibble(
  faucmic = ratio_grid,
  continuous = er_eval(mod_cure, cov_grid),
  cart = er_eval(mod_cart, cov_grid)
)
er_curve |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-faucmic, names_to = "model", values_to = "p") |>
  ggplot(aes(faucmic, 100 * p, linetype = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 28, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "fAUC0-24/MIC (h)", y = "Probability of clinical cure (%)", linetype = NULL)
```

```{r er-checks}
pts <- data.frame(AUC_GARENOXACIN = c(1, 28, 1000) / 0.25, MIC = 1)
p_cont <- er_eval(mod_cure, pts)
round(100 * p_cont, 1)
# Figure 5 curve read at 1, 28 (the CART circle) and 1000 h: about 39, 75 and
# 94%. The curve is deterministic, so the tolerance only covers digitisation.
stopifnot(all(abs(100 * p_cont - c(39, 75, 94)) < 2))

p_cart <- er_eval(mod_cart, data.frame(AUC_GARENOXACIN = c(20, 200) / 0.25, MIC = 1))
round(100 * p_cart, 1)
# Table 5: 2/5 cured at or below the split, 56/61 above it.
stopifnot(abs(p_cart - c(2 / 5, 56 / 61)) < 5e-4)
```

## Cure probability in the simulated phase III cohort

Combining the two layers as the paper did (final-model AUC0-24 with each
patient's MIC) shows how cure probability depends on the pathogen's
susceptibility at 400 mg once daily. The individual AUC is taken as dose /
CL/F, the exact steady-state AUC0-24 of the simulated subject.

```{r cohort-cure}
auc_ind <- sim_p3 |> distinct(id, cl) |> mutate(AUC_GARENOXACIN = 400 / cl)
mics <- c(0.06, 0.25, 1, 4, 32)
cure_tab <- lapply(mics, function(m) {
  p <- er_eval(mod_cure, data.frame(AUC_GARENOXACIN = auc_ind$AUC_GARENOXACIN, MIC = m))
  data.frame(MIC = m, median_p = median(p),
             pct_target = 100 * mean(0.25 * auc_ind$AUC_GARENOXACIN / m > 30))
}) |> bind_rows()
cure_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("MIC (ug/mL)" = MIC, "Median P(cure)" = median_p,
                "fAUC0-24/MIC > 30 h (%)" = pct_target) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Most phase III isolates had an MIC at or below 0.06 ug/mL (Table 2), where the
predicted cure probability is above 90%, consistent with the 87.9% observed
cure rate in the 66-patient PK/PD set. *P. aeruginosa* (MIC up to 32 ug/mL)
falls well below the 30 h target, matching the 2 of 5 cures in Table 7.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Interim CLCR centring.** Table 3 prints Model 2 as
  `CL/F = theta1 + theta2 x (CLCR - 85)` while Table 4 prints
  `(CLCR - 102)`. Methods Eq. 3 defines the centring value as the arithmetic
  mean of the covariate in the population, which was 102.4 mL/min in the
  phase I/II data set (Table 2) and 85 mL/min only in the pooled phase I-III
  set. The Figure 4 reproduction above also matches only with 102. The
  interim model therefore uses 102; Table 3's 85 is read as carried over from
  the final model.
* **Units.** CL/F intercepts and slopes are kept in the published mL/min and
  converted to L/h inside `model()`.
* **Sex coding.** The paper's GEN (1 = male) is encoded as `1 - SEXF`; the
  male additive V/F shift keeps its published sign.
* **CLCR.** Raw Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance in mL/min (not
  BSA-normalised), supplied in the canonical `CRCL` column.
* **IIV structure.** CL/F and V/F etas are correlated as reported; the ka eta
  is independent (Table 4 reports no covariance for it).
* **Unbound fraction.** fu = 0.25 comes from the Discussion (75% serum protein
  binding, cited from Van Wart et al.); the Methods do not restate it. It
  reproduces the paper's statement that AUC0-24/MIC 125 h is about fAUC0-24/MIC
  30 h, and the Table 7 Monte Carlo medians are of the size this fu implies.
* **AUC0-24 in the cure models.** The paper computed each patient's AUC0-24
  from the final population PK model (empirical Bayes); the models take it as
  a covariate column (`AUC_GARENOXACIN`, total concentration) so any source can
  be used. In this article it is dose / individual CL/F.
* **Residual error of the cure models.** The logistic regressions have a
  Bernoulli likelihood with no residual; a fixed placeholder additive SD of
  0.001 on the probability satisfies rxode2's need for an observation
  declaration.
* **Figure 3 and Table 7 Monte Carlo.** Not regenerated, because the pathogen
  MIC distributions are reported only as MIC90 and range.
* **Virtual cohorts.** Weight and CLCR are drawn independently from truncated
  log-normal distributions with the Table 2 means and SDs; the paper reports no
  joint distribution. For Figure 4 the 55 phase II CLCR values are
  represented by quantiles of a truncated normal distribution with the
  reported mean and SD.
* **Figure 6 reference values** are digitised medians, so the phase III NCA
  comparison is approximate.
